name: The traders in the temple
charge: Making the house of prayer a den of thieves
summary: Twice Christ found the temple court full of those that sold oxen, sheep, and doves, and the changers of money sitting. He made a scourge of small cords, drove them out, poured out the changers' money, overthrew the tables, and would not suffer any man to carry a vessel through the temple.
offense: Isaiah had called it a house of prayer for all people; Jeremiah had asked, is this house become a den of robbers in your eyes? The trade occupied the court of the Gentiles, the only place the nations could pray, and did it, on the gospel's account, for profit under the priests' patronage.
judgment: Driven out with a whip. The chief priests sought how they might destroy him for it. Zechariah's last verse hangs over the scene: in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite, the trafficker, in the house of the Lord of hosts.

lawsResolved.text: True worship and service to God requires not formalism or excessive piety but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God.
Priests are to keep the charge of the sanctuary and tabernacle of the congregation and keep it supplied and in proper order.
Corruption is the way of those who are greedy of gain.
You shall not bring the hire of a harlot or the wages of a dog (male prostitute) into the house of the LORD your God for any pledge, vow or tithe.

text.text: And the Jews’ passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem,
And found in the temple those that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting:
And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew the tables;
And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.
And his disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
And Jesus went into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,
And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.

And they come to Jerusalem: and Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves;
And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple.
And he taught, saying unto them, Is it not written, My house shall be called of all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.
And the scribes and chief priests heard it, and sought how they might destroy him: for they feared him, because all the people was astonished at his doctrine.

Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the Lord.

Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness unto the Lord of hosts: and all they that sacrifice shall come and take of them, and seethe therein: and in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts.
For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.
